newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe's industrial index slows fall.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe's industrial index slows fall.

text.p: Zimbabwe's industrial shares on Tuesday recorded their lowest fall in two weeks of declines, a development ascribed by brokers to improving sentiment.

The key industrial index, in decline since its April 24 record high of 10,980.10, shed 13.33 points or 0.13 percent to close at 10,242.92 but for the first time in weeks climbers out-numbered decliners at 14 to eight.
"It looks like things are steadying up a bit as interest rates have stopped going the other direction," Trudy Cashel, a director with Quincor James Capel told Reuters.

Short-term rates on the money market have risen more than six percent in the last few weeks on fears inflation is on the rise again, after a recent bout of price increases ahead of the government budget.
"There is a view that inflation will remain above 20 percent for the next month or two as the (central) Reserve Bank tries to keep rates positive as demanded by the IMF," Cashel said.

On Tuesday gains were seen in transporters Clan and tyre manufacturers Dunlop both 10 cents to 120 and 160 respectively, drug manufacturers Caps rose 25 to 1,725 and wine manufacturers Cairns added 50 to 1,600 cents.

A special bargain in bankers NMB lifted the share 50 cents to 3,400 while sugar manufacturers ZSR ZSR.ZI also added 50 to 1,350. Down were multi-industrialists TZI TZI.ZI off by 10 to 1,000 while bankers FMB dropped 300 to 4,000 cents.

Activity also returned to the mining index with declines in gold counters Falgold, minus five to 55 and Falcon down 200 to 1,200 while Ashanti traded unchanged at 9,000 cents, nicking 1.40 from the index to 987.01.
Wankie, which recently posted reasonable results, continued its journey up, firming 10 cents to 530.
